title: First Responder: SDK Debug Diffs & Quick-Triage Cheatsheet
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic "first responder" cheat sheet for engineers who get paged for SDK-related issues (client libraries, integration regressions, or unexpected errors seen in customer sandboxes). Goal: triage to a reproducible minimal test, identify likely root cause buckets, and hand off a prioritized next action list (fix/mitigate/rollback).

When to use:
- Customer repro or internal smoke tests failing after a SDK or runtime change.
- Latency/serialization regressions that appear SDK-bound.
- Error surface increases (400/500 spikes) that correlate with a recent release or feature flag.

Quick triage checklist (first 12 minutes):
1) Confirm alert context (1–2 min)
   - Which SDK (js/py/go/rust)? Which version? Get exact package version string.
   - Where seen: staging/production/dedicated/private? Region? Customer name (if any).
   - Short reproduction steps from reporter (copy/paste).

2) Reproduce minimally (3–6 min)
   - Try the simplest request that replicates failure: copy rpc/curl/SDK call and run locally with --verbose.
   - If network differences suspected, run from a cloud shell in same region and from local dev machine.
   - Use captured headers and body; keep auth tokens redacted.

3) Check telemetry & logs (parallel)
   - Client-side: check SDK logs (trace/debug) for stack traces, serialization errors, or tokenization warnings.
   - Server-side: look at request_id, model, route, and latency percentiles (p50/p95) around the incident window.
   - Error codes: map 4xx vs 5xx vs timeouts — 4xx likely contract/validation; 5xx likely server or infra.

4) Quick root-cause buckets (decide top-2)
   - Version regression: new client changes (breaking API shape), dependency bump.
   - Serialization/encoding: newline escaping, JSON schema drift, proto mismatch, Base64 differences.
   - Tokenization/prompt formatting: model receives different token lengths, special tokens removed/added.
   - Network/timeouts: default timeout change, keepalive behavior, DNS/regional routing.
   - Batching/caching behavior: new batching strategy increased latency or reordering, KV cache invalidation.
   - Environment/config drift: feature-flag toggles, environment variables, API key scopes.

Rapid evidence collection (commands & quick snippets):
- Curl (reproduce server request):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"x-small","prompt":"hello"}' -v -sS -D -

- Python minimal client run (vebose):
  python -c "from redwood_sdk import Client; c=Client(token='REDACT'); print(c.generate('hello', model='x-small'))"

- Compare request bytes (if suspect encoding):
  echo '{"prompt":"\nHello\u00A0"}' | xxd | head

Heuristics for quick diffing between versions:
- If stack trace points to a client module (e.g., client/transport/http.py) — suspect transport or header shaping.
- If errors only on long prompts — suspect tokenization/kv-cache/attention/window.
- If failure only after N requests in a session — suspect streaming/kv-cache lifecycle or session token leak.
- If errors correlated to region — suspect smart routing/fallback or model variant mapping.

Minimal A/B test to isolate SDK vs service (10–30 min):
- Use old binary: run same request with older SDK version pinned (docker: python:3.10 + pip install redwood-sdk==X.Y.Z) from same machine. If older works, likely client-regression.
- If both fail from local dev but succeed from a different network/region instance, suspect network/routing.

Common quick fixes and mitigations (ordered by impact & cost):
- Rollback the recent SDK deploy or unpublish the problematic client release.
- Feature flag disable (if new batching/cache enabled) to restore previous behavior.
- Short-term client-side retry/backoff changes to reduce error amplification.
- Patch: fix JSON encoding of non-UTF chars, escape sequences, or header normalization.

When to escalate to serving/runtime or infra SRE:
- 5xx spikes across many customers and models — escalate immediately to infra/sre with timeframe & p95 latency.
- Persistent divergence in model output quality after client fix — escalate to applied-ml for evals and prompt regression analysis.
- Cross-region network partitions or DNS flaps — SRE/infra to investigate.

Evidence to include in the ticket before handoff:
- Minimal reproducible script (curl/python) + exact SDK version used.
- Request_id(s), timestamps, p50/p95 latency snapshots, sample request payload (redacted).
- Diff of bytes where applicable (xxd outputs) and any non-ASCII characters found.
- Short hypothesis (one line) and next three recommended actions.

Developer tips: diagnosing tricky failure modes
- Tokenization mismatch: compare tokenizer outputs between SDK and server tokenizer (dump token ids). If tokens differ, check tokenizer version/package.
- Streaming partials: enable client debug to capture chunk boundaries; check for off-by-one buffer flush that can change prompt framing.
- Batching regressions: if aggregated payloads exceed route input limit, server may return 413 or mis-handle request. Look for per-request token_count.

Experiment log (fast notes):
- 2025-08-12: initial draft of this checklist after DEVDX-421. Observed a JS SDK change that normalized newlines and introduced \n  replacement that broke a few doc-generation prompts.
- 2025-09-03: added xxd byte-diff step after seeing NBSP (\u00A0) causing token discrepancies.
- 2025-11-18: added A/B quickpin workflow (old SDK container) to enable very short validation loop during incidents.

Integration & follow-up (post-mortem checklist):
- If root cause is SDK bug: open a patch PR with tests reproducing the issue, link to incident ticket, assign to SDK owner.
- Add a targeted unit/integration test to CI: encoding roundtrip tests, streaming chunk boundaries, and a long-prompt regression test.
- Add a short playbook blurb to SDK release notes: known incompatibilities, recommended pinning behavior.
- Add telemetry/metric if missing: client-side encoding error counter, per-session chunk-error rate, SDK-version skew in error rates.

Slack & pager conventions (what to post while triaging):
- Post short updates to #oncall-devexp: one-liner status (reproduced/mitigated/escalated) + ticket link.
- If customer-facing, coordinate with CS: include safe reproducible steps and ETA for next update.

Open questions / TODOs (near term):
- Build a tiny 'incident toolkit' docker image that can spin up pinned SDK versions and run smoke-cases in <2 min. (owner: Jonah)
- Add an automated byte-diff artifact to our request logging pipeline (owner: Priya).
- Make common curl + python reproducer snippets available in a central support snippet library.

Appendix: quick checklist card (printable)
- 1: get exact SDK version + region + repro steps
- 2: reproduce with curl/python locally and in-cloud
- 3: check client logs & server request_id/latency
- 4: isolate bucket (version/encoding/network/batching)
- 5: run A/B with pinned old SDK if available
- 6: apply mitigation (rollback/flag/patch) and document

End of doc.

Notes to self: keep this <1 page when printed. Convert high-value snippets into a small incident-container image and link from next revision.
